title: From  ₹80,000 rent to  ₹2.5 lakh a month: Indian Woman in Sweden breaks down monthly budget in viral video
content:
• According to Kritika Sakoriya, an Indian woman in Sweden, a single person's realistic monthly budget ranges from 18,000 to 25,000 Swedish Krona (SEK), which is approximately ₹1.8 lakh to ₹2.5 lakh.
• Kritika Sakoriya detailed that monthly rent in Sweden can range from 8,000 to 15,000 Swedish Krona (SEK), roughly ₹80,000 to ₹1.5 lakh, depending on the city and accommodation.
• Another Indian woman named Jyoti noted that over the past ten years, living costs in Sweden, including rent, groceries, and electricity, have dramatically increased compared to when she first moved there.

title: Trump says US-Iran talks ‘going on right now’, calls it Tehran’s ‘last chance’ to reach deal
content:
• US President Donald Trump stated on Monday, August 3, that negotiations with Iran were underway, calling it Tehran's 'last chance' for a deal.
• The primary objectives of the US-Iran negotiations are to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and address Washington's concerns over Iran's nuclear programme.
• Trump outlined a two-stage roadmap for a potential agreement: first, the opening of the Strait of Hormuz, and second, denuclearization.

title: Govt looks to bring back merchant fee on UPI transactions
content:
• The finance ministry has proposed the "Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026" to amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, potentially allowing the reintroduction of Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions.
• The proposed amendment seeks to scrap Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, which currently prohibits banks and payment system providers (PSPs) from levying MDR on electronic payments.
• The government had banned MDR on UPI and RuPay debit card transactions from January 2020; the estimated subsidy payout for digital payments in the Budget for 2026-27 is ₹2,000 crore.

title: WhatsApp puts multiple accounts, including in India, under 24-hour review; users report sudden restrictions
content:
• WhatsApp placed multiple user accounts, including some in India, under a 24-hour review process on Monday, August 3, temporarily restricting access to all app features.
• The review, typically resolved within 24 hours, checks 'account activity and device info' to ensure compliance with WhatsApp's terms of service.
• A WhatsApp spokesperson acknowledged that while working to prevent misuse, mistakes can occur during the review process, which the company aims to fix quickly.

title: Trump seen as growing political liability by Senate Republicans ahead of 2026 midterms: Report
content:
• A proposed $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund, intended to compensate MAGA allies, was rescinded by Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and the Justice Department.
• The rescission of the $1.8 billion fund occurred after North Carolina Republican Sen. Thom Tillis and Texas Sen. John Cornyn threatened to block Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche's confirmation.
• President Trump continues to demand that the Senate pass the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE America) Act before the election.

title: ‘Bangalore feels cheaper’: 21-year-old shares  ₹43,000 monthly budget breakup while living alone in Gurgaon
content:
• A 21-year-old woman named Chahat Yadav, living alone in Gurgaon, reported a total monthly expenditure of ₹43,096 for July.
• The largest portion of her budget was rent, costing ₹15,000 per month for a fully furnished 1RK apartment.
• Other significant expenses for Chahat Yadav in July included ₹12,805 for shopping and ₹6,879 for groceries, food deliveries, and daily essentials, with the total expenditure excluding investments.

title: Iran's 'survival economy': Families sell empty perfume bottles, natural hair for income
content:
• Iran's annual inflation reached 66% in the Iranian month ending in late July.
• Year-on-year inflation in Iran stood at 87.9%, indicating severe economic hardship.
• The Statistical Center of Iran reported these inflation figures, while the ILNA news agency described the trend of families selling personal belongings as a "survival economy".

title: Why did Todd Blanche scrap Trump's $1.8 billion ‘anti-weaponization fund’ before attorney general confirmation vote?
content:
• Acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche formally terminated President Donald Trump's controversial $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization fund".
• Todd Blanche signed a formal order on Sunday rescinding the Justice Department's May 18, 2026 order that had originally established the anti-weaponization fund.
• The revised IRS settlement for Donald Trump narrows audit protection, applying it only retroactively to tax matters covered by the settlement and not preventing the IRS from examining future tax filings.

title: Bhaiyyaji Joshi steps down as Ram Temple Trust's patron, health cited as reason: Report
content:
• Senior RSS leader Suresh Bhaiyyaji Joshi has stepped down from his role as Palak (patron/guardian) of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, citing health reasons.
• Suresh Bhaiyyaji Joshi's role as Palak for the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust primarily involved organisational guidance and coordination, rather than day-to-day administration.
• Joshi was entrusted with the responsibility of Palak for the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust during a period when the Trust faced allegations over a controversial land purchase, with the objective of strengthening its functioning.

title: Government invites applications for 30 products' import quota under India-Oman trade pact
content:
• Applications for imports under the Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) for FY27 under the India-Oman trade pact are invited from August 4 to August 19, 2026.
• Under the trade pact, India will maintain zero import duty on up to 2,000 tonnes of dates per year, previously subject to a 30% duty.
• The import duty on marble and travertine blocks from Oman will fall from 40% to 25% for imports priced up to and above $150 per metric tonne, with an annual import quota of 1 lakh tonnes.
